newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian firm sees possible mazut export duty Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: Russian firm sees possible mazut export duty Jan 1.

text.p: Interfax news agency quoted an unnamed Russian oil company official as saying on Wednesday that Moscow may levy a tariff of up to 80,000 roubles per tonne on heavy fuel oil (mazut) exports from January 1, 1997.
Mazut traders are expecting some form of restrictions, but none have yet been forthcoming.
The Interfax report, which provided no new information, reflected continuing talk in Moscow that Russia plans to restrict mazut exports to bolster winter supplies.
Russia has in recent years raised heavy fuel oil export tariffs or banned deliveries abroad outright, which has conditioned traders to expect a restriction each winter.
But possible curbs are late in coming this year and there is still no clear signal from the government on what restrictions, if any, will be implemented and when.
